title: S3 Storage Classes Comparison
description: Decision framework for S3 Storage Classes based on access frequency, retrieval latency, minimum duration, and cost.

items.name: S3 Standard
items.description: Default high-durability object storage for active data.

features.bestFor: Frequently accessed data, dynamic websites, content distribution.

items.bestFor: Frequently accessed active data requiring instant access without retrieval charges.
items.avoidFor: Long-term archival data or data accessed less than once a month.

items.name: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
items.description: Auto-tiering based on access patterns with zero operational overhead.

features.bestFor: Data with unknown, changing, or unpredictable access patterns.

items.bestFor: Workloads with unknown or unpredictable access patterns without retrieval penalties.
items.avoidFor: Objects < 128KB (monitoring fee per object applies) or known access frequencies.

items.name: S3 Standard-IA
items.description: Infrequent access storage across multiple AZs.

features.bestFor: Long-term backups, disaster recovery files accessed < 1 time/month.

items.bestFor: Crucial backups and disaster recovery files requiring instant multi-AZ retrieval.
items.avoidFor: Files deleted within 30 days or accessed frequently.

items.name: S3 One Zone-IA
items.description: Lower cost Infrequent Access stored in a single AZ.

features.bestFor: Secondary backup copies, reproducible thumbnails, non-critical data.

items.bestFor: Re-creatable data or secondary backups when AZ resilience is not required.
items.avoidFor: Mission-critical data where AZ outage causes permanent data loss.

items.name: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval

features.bestFor: Medical records, news media archives accessed once per quarter.

items.bestFor: Archival data accessed once or twice a year requiring instant retrieval.
items.avoidFor: Data deleted within 90 days or frequent access.

items.name: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
items.description: Classic cold archive with expedited/standard/bulk retrieval tiers.

features.retrievalTime: Expedited (1-5 min), Standard (3-5 hr), Bulk (5-12 hr)
features.bestFor: Annual compliance archives, disaster recovery where minutes/hours delay is acceptable.

items.bestFor: Cost-effective archives where retrieval delay of 1-5 minutes to a few hours is acceptable.

items.name: S3 Glacier Deep Archive
items.description: Lowest cost cloud storage for long-term retention (7-10+ years).

features.bestFor: Regulatory compliance (HIPAA, SEC, financial records) stored 7-10 years.

items.bestFor: Long-term regulatory archival with acceptable retrieval delay of 12-48 hours.
items.avoidFor: Workloads requiring retrieval within the same business day.

title: Elastic Load Balancers (ALB vs NLB vs GWLB)
description: Selection guide for AWS Elastic Load Balancing based on OSI layer, protocol, throughput, and target types.

items.name: Application Load Balancer (ALB)

features.routingFeatures: Path-based (/api), Host-based, Query string, Header & Cookie routing, OIDC Auth
features.bestFor: Microservices, containerized apps (ECS/EKS), modern web applications.

items.bestFor: HTTP/HTTPS web applications requiring advanced routing rules, redirects, or container target groups.
items.avoidFor: Non-HTTP protocols (TCP/UDP), ultra-low sub-millisecond latency, or workloads needing static IP.

items.name: Network Load Balancer (NLB)
items.description: Layer 4 ultra-high performance load balancer capable of handling millions of requests/sec.

features.routingFeatures: Flow hash based routing, Source IP preservation
features.bestFor: Gaming, streaming, trading platforms, IoT, AWS PrivateLink targets.

items.bestFor: Workloads requiring static IP addresses, PrivateLink endpoints, TLS termination at Layer 4, or sub-millisecond speed.
items.avoidFor: Complex HTTP path/host routing or web application firewall header evaluation.

items.name: Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)
items.description: Deploy, scale, and manage 3rd party virtual network appliances (Firewalls, IDS/IPS, DPI).

features.osiLayer: Layer 3 Gateway + Layer 4 Balancer (GENEVE encapsulation on port 6081)
features.routingFeatures: Routes all IP traffic transparently through appliance fleets
features.bestFor: Palo Alto, Checkpoint, Fortinet firewalls, IDS/IPS traffic inspection.

items.bestFor: Deploying third-party virtual security inspection appliances in a centralized VPC architecture.

title: Database Engines (Aurora vs RDS vs DynamoDB vs ElastiCache)
description: Decision matrix for selecting the optimal AWS Database service based on data model, consistency, scaling, and operational overhead.

items.name: Amazon Aurora
items.description: Cloud-native enterprise relational database with 6-way storage replication across 3 AZs.

features.scaling: Auto-scaling storage (up to 128TB), up to 15 Read Replicas, Aurora Serverless v2
features.haDr: Sub-30s failover, 6 copies across 3 AZs, Global Database (<1s replication lag)
features.bestFor: Enterprise ERP, SaaS multi-tenant, high-throughput transactional OLTP.

items.bestFor: High-throughput relational applications demanding rapid automatic failover and massive read scaling.
items.avoidFor: Simple key-value lookup workloads or tight budget hobby projects.

items.name: Amazon RDS
items.description: Managed traditional relational databases (Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server).

features.scaling: Vertical instance resize, storage auto-scaling up to 64TB, up to 5-15 read replicas
features.haDr: Synchronous standby in secondary AZ (60-120s failover)
features.bestFor: Existing database migrations (Oracle/SQL Server), traditional line-of-business apps.

items.bestFor: Applications requiring specific legacy database engines or straightforward relational databases.
items.avoidFor: Serverless applications with erratic spiky connection spikes without Proxy.

items.name: Amazon DynamoDB
items.description: Fully managed serverless NoSQL key-value and document database with single-digit millisecond latency.

features.scaling: On-Demand mode or Provisioned auto-scaling (Virtually unlimited scale)
features.bestFor: Mobile backends, gaming leaderboards, shopping carts, session stores, IoT telemetry.

items.bestFor: High-scale, serverless workloads requiring single-digit millisecond read/write latencies at any scale.
items.avoidFor: Complex multi-table JOINs, analytics ad-hoc aggregations, or strict relational graphs.

items.name: Amazon ElastiCache & MemoryDB
items.description: In-memory caching and ultra-fast data store (Redis / Memcached).

features.dataModel: In-Memory Key-Value, Data Structures (Hashes, Sets, Sorted Sets)
features.bestFor: Session management, database query result caching, pub/sub messaging, real-time leaderboards.

items.bestFor: Offloading read pressure from relational databases and achieving microsecond response times.
items.avoidFor: Primary persistent source of truth storage without persistent backup.

title: Storage Solutions (EBS vs EFS vs FSx vs S3)
description: Comparison matrix of AWS Storage options by protocol, attachment mode, file system type, and performance.

items.name: Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS)
items.description: Block storage volumes dedicated to a single EC2 instance within the same AZ.

features.attachment: Single EC2 instance (Multi-Attach available on io1/io2 in same AZ)
features.performance: Up to 256,000 IOPS and 4,000 MB/s per volume (io2 Block Express)
features.bestFor: Boot volumes, database data files, single instance low-latency disk.

items.bestFor: High-performance block storage for OS roots and relational database data files.
items.avoidFor: Shared file access across multiple instances in different AZs.

items.name: Amazon Elastic File System (EFS)
items.description: Serverless, elastic NFS shared file system across multiple AZs for Linux workloads.

features.storageScope: Regional (Multi-AZ by default, One Zone optional)
features.attachment: Concurrent mount from 1,000s of Linux EC2, ECS, EKS, Lambda instances
features.performance: Elastic throughput (scales automatically) or Provisioned up to 3+ GB/s
features.bestFor: Shared web serving (WordPress), container shared persistent storage, CI/CD home dirs.

items.bestFor: Linux workloads requiring shared concurrent file access across multiple AZs and compute services.
items.avoidFor: Windows file systems (CIFS/SMB) or high IOPS OLTP databases.

items.name: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
items.description: Fully managed native Microsoft Windows file storage built on Windows Server.

features.attachment: Concurrent mount from Windows and Linux instances via SMB, Active Directory integrated
features.performance: Up to 2+ GB/s throughput and 100,000+ IOPS with in-memory caching
features.bestFor: Enterprise Windows apps, Active Directory file shares, SQL Server Failover Clusters (FCI).

items.bestFor: Native Windows application migrations and Active Directory integrated file shares.

items.name: Amazon FSx for Lustre
items.description: High-performance compute (HPC) file system optimized for fast processing of big data and ML.

features.attachment: Seamless bi-directional synchronization with Amazon S3 buckets
features.performance: Sub-millisecond latencies, hundreds of GB/s throughput, millions of IOPS
features.bestFor: Machine learning training (SageMaker), financial modeling, genomics, video rendering.

items.bestFor: High-performance computing and machine learning workloads connected directly with S3.
items.avoidFor: Standard office document sharing or long-term cold archives.
